name: com.viralvideosearch/viralvideosearch
title: ViralVideoSearch
description: Find viral short-form videos and get step-by-step recreation plans: hooks, shot lists, scripts.

tools.name: search_viral_videos
tools.description: Search the videos collected by the caller's own searches on the VVS website (only the caller's rows; not the shared VVS corpus and not bookmarks) for a caption substring, case-insensitive, sorted by views. Use list_viral_videos instead when there is no search text or you need bookmarked videos (source=saved). Use search_corpus_videos to search the public English-only corpus by caption or hashtag, and use find_outliers, find_winning_hooks or the other niche tools to research a niche. Pass a result's id to get_my_video_details or get_my_video_analysis. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

query.description: Text to match anywhere in the caption (case-insensitive substring, not keywords or regex; % and _ act as wildcards).

platform.description: Only return videos from this platform. Omit for all platforms.

tools.name: list_viral_videos
tools.description: List the caller's own videos, newest first, with offset pagination. All three source options return only the caller's data: mine (default) = videos collected by the caller's website searches; saved = videos the caller bookmarked with save_video, which can include shared-corpus videos; all = both, de-duplicated. Use search_viral_videos instead to match caption text, get_my_video_details for one collected video's full record, and find_outliers instead to browse the shared VVS corpus by niche. For a bookmarked shared-corpus video, use get_corpus_video_analysis instead of get_my_video_details or get_my_video_analysis, because those two only accept videos the caller collected. Returns {count, videos:[{id, platform, caption, source_url, creator_username, play_count, like_count, search_query, created_at}]} (saved/all rows add saved_at and notes); count below limit means you reached the end. Read-only. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

platform.description: Only list videos from this platform. Omit for all platforms.

source.description: mine = videos collected by your own website searches (current behavior); saved = videos bookmarked with save_video, newest saved first, rows add saved_at and notes; all = both, de-duplicated, newest first

offset.description: Number of videos to skip for pagination (use the previous offset + limit).

tools.name: get_my_video_details
tools.description: Fetch the full stored record (platform, caption, source_url, creator, view/like/comment/share counts, search_query, timestamps) of one video the caller collected through their own website searches. Ids from search_viral_videos or list_viral_videos source=mine. Use get_my_video_analysis instead when you need the AI breakdown (hook, scenes, transcript), list_my_analyses to see which of the caller's videos are analyzed, and get_corpus_video_analysis or get_recreation_plan instead for shared-corpus videos (ids from find_outliers and other niche tools, or corpus bookmarks), which return {error:"not_found"} here. Returns the video record, or {error:"not_found"} if the caller did not collect that id. Read-only. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

id.description: Video id (UUID) from search_viral_videos or list_viral_videos results.

tools.name: get_my_video_analysis
tools.description: Return the stored AI breakdown of one video the caller collected through their own website searches. It only reads an existing analysis: it never starts one or spends credits. Use get_my_video_details instead for the video's metadata and counts, list_my_analyses to see which of the caller's videos are analyzed, get_corpus_video_analysis for shared-corpus videos (ids from find_outliers, search_corpus_videos and other niche tools), and get_recreation_plan when the user wants a shot list and script to remake a video. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

video_id.description: Saved-library video id (UUID): the id from search_viral_videos/list_viral_videos, or viral_video_id from list_my_analyses.

tools.name: list_my_analyses
tools.description: List the AI analyses of videos the caller collected through their own website searches, newest first, with offset pagination, one summary row per analysis (hook, style, format, angle, confidence). Use it to see which of the caller's videos are analyzed or to compare their hooks. Use get_my_video_analysis instead (with viral_video_id) for one full breakdown, get_my_video_details for a video's metadata, and get_corpus_video_analysis instead for shared-corpus videos. Returns {count, analyses:[{id, viral_video_id, hook_text, hook_style, format_type, emotional_angle, cta_style, confidence, created_at}]}; count below limit means you reached the end. Read-only. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

offset.description: Number of analyses to skip for pagination (previous offset + limit).

tools.name: list_niches
tools.description: List every niche in the shared VVS corpus with its slug, label, video_count, analyzed_count, platforms (video count per platform) and last_capture_at. Call it first in a session to get valid niche slugs for find_outliers, find_winning_hooks, find_rising_formats, find_rising_sounds, find_breakout_creators, watch_niche and save_brand_profile_and_skill, and to check data freshness (last_capture_at). Returns {count, note, niches:[...]}; results are cached for up to 10 minutes. Read-only, no parameters. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

tools.name: find_outliers
tools.description: Find the shared-corpus videos in one niche that most beat their baseline, ranked by outlier_score (views ÷ the creator's own median when VVS has 3+ of their videos, otherwise ÷ the niche or platform median; see baseline_source), never by raw views. Use it to answer "what is over-performing in <niche>". Use search_corpus_videos instead to search the public English-only corpus by caption or hashtag across niches. Use find_winning_hooks instead for opening lines only, find_breakout_creators for accounts rather than videos, analyze_creator for one named creator, and search_viral_videos for the caller's own collected videos. Free accounts get 5 rows with only hook_text and format_type, plus upgrade_url. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

min_multiple.description: Minimum baseline-backed views multiple; defaults to 1.0.

niche.description: Niche slug from list_niches, e.g. "personal-finance". Labels such as "Personal Finance" are also accepted; an unknown niche returns an error listing valid slugs.

platform.description: Only this platform. Omit for all.

days.description: Only videos posted in the last N days.

max_followers.description: Only creators at or below this follower count. When set, creators with unknown follower counts (most Instagram accounts) are excluded. Omit for no ceiling.

format_type.description: Only formats containing this text (case-insensitive substring), e.g. "talking head", "pov", "tutorial". Omit for all formats.

tools.name: find_breakout_creators
tools.description: Find small creators in one niche who repeatedly beat the niche median (videos at 2× niche median or more), sorted by outlier count. Use it to find accounts worth studying. Use find_outliers instead for individual videos and analyze_creator instead to study one named creator in depth. Returns {niche, days, max_followers, min_outliers, data_as_of, creators:[{handle, platform, followers, outlier_count, videos_in_window, usual_views_median, videos_in_corpus, baseline_confidence, best_video:{video_id, source_url, views, x_niche_median, hook_text, format_type}}], empty_reason?}; when nothing qualifies, empty_reason suggests a lower min_outliers. Free accounts get 5 rows with only hook_text and format_type, plus upgrade_url. Read-only. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

niche.description: Niche slug from list_niches, e.g. "personal-finance". Labels such as "Personal Finance" are also accepted; an unknown niche returns an error listing valid slugs.

max_followers.description: Follower ceiling for a creator to count as small.

min_outliers.description: Minimum number of the creator's videos at 2× niche median or more.

days.description: Only videos posted in the last N days.

include_unknown_followers.description: Also include creators whose follower count is unknown (most Instagram accounts).

tools.name: analyze_creator
tools.description: Analyze one named creator's videos in the shared VVS corpus against their own median views: ranked videos (x_own_median), their top 3 vs bottom 3, and which hook style, format, pacing and duration differ. Use it when the user names a specific handle. Use find_breakout_creators instead to discover creators worth studying, and find_outliers instead for niche-wide videos. Without platform it uses the platform where VVS has the most of their videos. Returns {handle, platform, videos_in_corpus, other_platforms, followers, own_median_views, ranking, top_outliers, bottom_videos, what_differs:[...], videos:[...]}; with 0 videos it returns a message and no teardown, and with 1–2 videos it lists them without drawing conclusions. Free accounts get 5 rows with only hook_text and format_type, plus upgrade_url. what_differs is paid-only. Read-only. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

handle.description: Creator handle, with or without the leading @ (case-insensitive).

platform.description: Only this platform; set it when the same handle exists on several platforms.

tools.name: find_winning_hooks
tools.description: Return the exact opening hooks (first spoken or on-screen line) of the best-performing videos with a known hook in one niche, plus which hook style wins by median outlier_score with sample sizes. Use it when the user wants hook lines or hook styles to copy. Use find_outliers instead for whole videos and find_rising_formats instead for video structures. Only videos with a hook_text (analyzed) count. winning_hook_style and hook_styles are paid-only. Free accounts get 5 rows with only hook_text and format_type, plus upgrade_url. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

niche.description: Niche slug from list_niches, e.g. "personal-finance". Labels such as "Personal Finance" are also accepted; an unknown niche returns an error listing valid slugs.

days.description: Only videos posted in the last N days; widen to 30–60 if empty.

tools.name: find_rising_formats
tools.description: List up to 10 video formats in one niche whose stage is new or rising, from week-over-week counts and median velocity over the last 4 weeks, each with 3 example videos and the traits that stay constant (pacing, hook style, duration, structure). Use it to answer "what format should I try next"; use find_winning_hooks instead for opening lines, find_rising_sounds for audio, and find_outliers for single videos. Returns {niche, days, stage_as_of, stage_counts_in_niche, formats:[{format_type, stage, weekly_counts, median_velocity, stays_constant, examples_outside_window, examples:[...]}], empty_reason?}; stays_constant is paid-only. Free accounts get 5 rows with only hook_text and format_type, plus upgrade_url. Read-only. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

niche.description: Niche slug from list_niches, e.g. "personal-finance". Labels such as "Personal Finance" are also accepted; an unknown niche returns an error listing valid slugs.

days.description: Window in days for the example videos (stage is always computed over the last 4 weeks).

include_peaking.description: Also return formats already at their peak stage, not just new and rising ones.

tools.name: find_rising_sounds
tools.description: List sounds (audio tracks) used recently in one niche whose use across VVS is new or rising while still low (at or below max_uses), each with a stage, total uses in VVS, and an example video. TikTok and Instagram only; YouTube has no sound data. Use it to pick trending audio early. Use find_rising_formats instead for video structures and find_outliers for videos. Free accounts get 5 rows with only hook_text and format_type, plus upgrade_url. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

niche.description: Niche slug from list_niches, e.g. "personal-finance". Labels such as "Personal Finance" are also accepted; an unknown niche returns an error listing valid slugs.

days.description: Only videos posted in the last N days.

max_uses.description: Only sounds with at most this many total uses across VVS (keeps results early-stage).

include_original.description: Include creator-original audio, not just reusable sounds.

tools.name: get_corpus_video_analysis
tools.description: Return the full AI breakdown of one shared-corpus video: video_id from find_outliers, search_corpus_videos, find_winning_hooks, analyze_creator, find_breakout_creators, get_watch_report or a corpus bookmark. Use get_my_video_analysis instead for videos the caller collected through their own searches, and get_recreation_plan instead when the user wants the step-by-step shot list, script and filming guide. Reports the caller has already unlocked return in full; locked reports return a teaser (free accounts also get upgrade_url). Paid accounts can pass unlock=true to spend 1 plan analysis (or 1 credit) on a locked report, exactly like the website; repeating the call after unlocking does not charge again. Videos not yet analyzed return available:false with analyze_url. Errors on unknown or non-English videos. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

video_id.description: Shared-corpus video_id (UUID) from search_corpus_videos or find_outliers results.

unlock.description: Paid accounts only. true spends 1 plan analysis or credit to unlock a locked report. Set it only when the user explicitly asks to unlock.

tools.name: save_brand_profile_and_skill
tools.description: Save (replace) the caller's brand profile (niche, audience, competitors, voice notes, banned words, offer, own handles), generate a SKILL.md from it that tells the assistant which VVS tools to use for this brand and to write in its voice, store that SKILL.md with the profile, and return both. Each call replaces the whole saved profile (omitted fields become empty). The niche must be a valid list_niches slug, and it is validated before anything is written. Use get_my_brand_profile instead to read the saved profile without changing it, and watch_niche instead to monitor niches. Returns {saved, niche, profile, skill_md, how_to_save}. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

niche.description: Niche slug from list_niches, e.g. "personal-finance". Labels such as "Personal Finance" are also accepted; an unknown niche returns an error listing valid slugs.

voice_notes.description: Tone and voice to write in.

never_use_words.description: Words or phrases the assistant must never use.

offer.description: The product, service or offer the content promotes.

tools.name: get_my_brand_profile
tools.description: Read the caller's saved brand profile (niche, audience, competitors, voice notes, banned words, offer, own handles), the SKILL.md stored with it, the caller's plan tier (free or paid) and a short summary of their niche watches (niche, keywords, competitors, last_report_at). Use it to personalize answers. Use save_brand_profile_and_skill instead to create or change the profile, list_watched_niches instead when you need the watches with created/updated times and slot usage (10 max), and get_watch_report instead for what is new in watched niches. Returns {profile, watches, tier}, or {profile:null, watches, message} when no profile exists yet. Read-only, no parameters. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

tools.name: watch_niche
tools.description: Start or update a watch on one niche, with optional keywords and competitor handles, so get_watch_report can summarize what is new there. Use it to set up recurring monitoring; use get_watch_report to read results and list_watched_niches to see current watches. Calling it again for the same niche replaces that watch's keywords and competitors. Up to 10 niches per account; use unwatch_niche to stop watching. It reuses VVS's daily collection and never starts new scraping. Returns {watching:{niche, keywords, competitors}, next}. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

niche.description: Niche slug from list_niches, e.g. "personal-finance". Labels such as "Personal Finance" are also accepted; an unknown niche returns an error listing valid slugs.

keywords.description: Keywords to highlight in the report (matched against captions and hooks).

competitors.description: Competitor handles to track for new outliers, with or without @.

tools.name: get_watch_report
tools.description: Build a report for the caller's watched niches (up to 5) covering everything captured since that niche's previous report, or the last `days` days for a first report: top 8 outliers, keyword matches, winning hook styles and formats, breakout creators (2+ videos at 2× niche median, 50,000 followers or fewer) and new outliers from watched competitors. Use it for weekly monitoring after watch_niche; for one-off research use find_outliers. Each call marks the report time, so the next call only covers newer videos. Returns {reports:[{niche, since, data_as_of, new_videos_captured, top_outliers, keyword_matches, winning_hook_styles, winning_formats, find_breakout_creators, breakout_rule, competitor_new_outliers, watched_competitors, empty_reason?}]}; winning_hook_styles is paid-only. Free accounts get up to 5 rows per list with only hook_text and format_type, plus upgrade_url. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

days.description: Window in days used only when a niche has no previous report.

niche.description: Only report on this watched niche (slug from list_niches). Omit for all watched niches.

tools.name: get_recreation_plan
tools.description: Get the step-by-step recreation plan (the VVS playbook) for one video: hook, why it worked, scene-by-scene shot list with timings, script, filming guide and AI prompts. Pass exactly one of video_id (from find_outliers, search_corpus_videos or another VVS tool) or url (any public TikTok, Instagram or YouTube link, even one VVS has not seen). Use it when the user wants to remake a video. Use get_corpus_video_analysis instead for the raw breakdown of a shared-corpus video, get_my_video_analysis for a breakdown of a video the caller collected, and get_recreation_plan_status to poll a job it started. Already-unlocked plans return free. For a video VVS has already analyzed, a locked plan returns a teaser unless unlock=true, which spends 1 unlock (plan analysis or credit) exactly like the website; free accounts can reuse cached analyses this way. Starting a new analysis (a video VVS has not analyzed yet) is paid-only: paid accounts get confirmation_required first, and unlock=true then starts an analysis job; poll get_recreation_plan_status with job_id every 20–30 seconds (usually 1–3 minutes). Free accounts get status paid_only with upgrade_url for a video that has not been analyzed, and nothing is started or charged. Failed analyses are refunded. job_id can be null when another request is already analyzing the video (then call get_recreation_plan again later). Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

video_id.description: VVS video id (UUID) from find_outliers, find_winning_hooks or another VVS tool result. Pass this or url, not both.

url.description: Public TikTok, Instagram (Reel/post) or YouTube (Shorts/watch) link. Pass this or video_id, not both.

unlock.description: true spends 1 unlock (plan analysis or credit) on a locked plan, exactly like the website Unlock button. Set it only when the user explicitly asks to unlock.

tools.name: get_recreation_plan_status
tools.description: Check a recreation-plan job started by get_recreation_plan. Use it only with a job_id from that tool, polling every 20–30 seconds; for a video with no job, call get_recreation_plan instead. Returns status processing, ready (with the full plan), failed (with whether it was charged and refunded) or ready_to_unlock, plus credits and plan analyses remaining. Never spends credits. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

tools.name: save_video
tools.description: Bookmark one video into the caller's website Library (the Saved tab) by video_id, optionally with a private note. Use it when the user wants to keep a video found with find_outliers, find_winning_hooks, analyze_creator or another VVS tool; use remove_saved_video to undo it and list_viral_videos with source="saved" to list bookmarks. Saving a video that is already saved changes nothing (if notes is passed, the note is replaced). It only creates a bookmark: it never copies, re-scrapes or analyzes the video and costs no credits. Only shared-corpus videos and the caller's own videos can be saved; anything else returns {error:"not_found"}. Returns {saved:true, already_saved, video_id, saved_at, notes}. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

video_id.description: video_id (UUID) from find_outliers, find_winning_hooks, analyze_creator, find_breakout_creators, get_watch_report, or id from list_viral_videos/search_viral_videos.

notes.description: Optional private note stored with the bookmark. Omit to leave an existing note unchanged.

tools.name: remove_saved_video
tools.description: Delete the caller's bookmark for one video from their website Library (the Saved tab). Use it when the user no longer wants a video saved with save_video; it does not delete the video itself, its analysis, or videos the caller collected through their own website searches, and affects no other user. Removing a video that is not saved is a no-op and returns removed:false. Returns {removed, video_id}. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

video_id.description: video_id (UUID) of the saved video, as returned by save_video or list_viral_videos with source="saved".

tools.name: unwatch_niche
tools.description: Delete the caller's watch on one niche, including its keywords, competitor handles and report history (last_report_at), so get_watch_report stops covering it. Use it when the user wants to stop monitoring a niche or free one of their 10 watch slots; use watch_niche to change keywords or competitors instead of deleting. Unwatching a niche that is not watched is a no-op and returns removed:false. Does not touch the brand profile or other watches. Returns {removed, niche, watches_remaining}. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

niche.description: Niche slug from list_niches or list_watched_niches, e.g. "personal-finance". Labels are also accepted.

tools.name: list_watched_niches
tools.description: List the niches the caller is watching, with each watch's keywords, competitor handles, last_report_at and created/updated times, plus how many of the 10 watch slots are used. Use it before watch_niche, unwatch_niche or get_watch_report to check what is monitored. Use get_my_brand_profile instead when you need the brand profile and SKILL.md, and get_watch_report instead for the new videos in those niches. Returns {count, max_watches:10, watches:[{niche_slug, keywords, competitors, last_report_at, created_at, updated_at}]}; an empty list means nothing is watched yet. Read-only, no parameters. Requires a VVS API key or OAuth; 60 calls/minute per account.

tools.name: search_corpus_videos
tools.description: Search the public, English-only ViralVideoSearch corpus of analyzed and tracked short-form videos by caption or hashtag, ranked by outlier multiple then views. Use find_outliers instead when the user already has a niche slug and wants videos that beat a baseline in that niche, not a keyword search. Use search_viral_videos / list_viral_videos for the caller's own collected searches or saved videos. Each result includes an outlier multiple with baseline_label ("vs creator's usual views" when it is that creator's own median over at least 3 tracked videos, otherwise "vs niche median" or "vs platform median") and followers when known. Free callers always receive the top 5 (offset ignored) with remaining_count and upgrade_url; paid callers, credit-pack buyers and admins can page with offset and next_offset. Never starts an analysis, scrapes, or spends credits. Requires an API key or OAuth; the existing 60 calls/minute limit applies.

query.description: Caption phrase or hashtag to match; 2–100 characters.

platform.description: Restrict to this platform; omit for all.

offset.description: Paid callers only: skip this many ranked matches (use next_offset). Ignored for free callers.

limit.description: Maximum matches before the free top-five cap.
